title: Millet-snack brand cut quick-commerce dependence from 78% to 45% and tripled repeat orders in 90 days
content: A Bengaluru millet-snack brand was at ₹1.2 Cr/month GMV with 78% of it locked into Blinkit and Zepto. The platform economics were quietly killing them: ~22% commission, ~6% fulfilment, plus forced buy-1-get-1 during platform sale events. Blended contribution margin sat at just 9%, and they owned zero customer data — every reorder was rented back at full CAC. So they ran a 90-day own-the-customer push. Every quick-commerce shipment carried a QR insert offering ₹75 off the first direct order on their Shopify store, captured via WhatsApp opt-in. They retargeted Blinkit-heavy pin codes on Meta at ₹3.2L/month, driving to a Subscribe-and-Save pack (10% off, free shipping above ₹599), and ran WhatsApp reorder reminders at day 21. Blinkit was kept only for discovery SKUs; bulk packs moved to Amazon.in and direct. Over 90 days direct+Amazon climbed from 22% to 55% of GMV, quick-commerce fell to 45%, blended margin rose 9%→23%, repeat-order rate tripled 11%→34%, and the WhatsApp list hit 41,000 opted-in buyers.
lesson: Quick-commerce is a paid discovery channel, not a relationship. Pay to get found once, then use the QR insert plus a WhatsApp opt-in to convert that platform buyer into an owned, direct relationship — so you never pay 28% platform take to re-acquire the same customer on every reorder.
